In httpx 0.28.0, the deprecated `proxies` argument was removed. The search results show this in the release notes, which list it among several other changes that came with the release (the deprecated proxies argument has now been removed, per the 0.28.0 notes). The same release also deprecated the string form of `verify` and the `cert` argument, and it removed the `app` argument.

The replacement path goes back to 0.26.0. That release added a `proxy` argument and deprecated `proxies`, and its notes advised using the proxy argument instead of the deprecated proxies, or using mounts= for more complex configurations.

So for your migration:

- **Simple single-proxy setups:** replace `proxies=...` with `proxy=...` on the client.
- **Per-scheme or per-host routing:** use `mounts=` with transport objects that carry the proxy settings. The results don't include a code sample for this, so check the httpx advanced docs for the exact transport syntax. From memory, it looks roughly like `httpx.Client(mounts={"all://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy=...)})`, but verify that against the docs.

I didn't find a source for the exact migration code, so treat the mounts example as unverified until you check the current httpx documentation.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

input.prompt: Quote the exact documented syntax for configuring a proxy on httpx.Client: the `proxy=` argument, `mounts=` with HTTPTransport(proxy=...), and the mount key formats (e.g. "https://", "all://"). Also note any statement about the removed `proxies` argument and the version it applies to.
Find the 0.28.0 section and the 0.26.0 section. Quote the entries about the `proxies` argument (deprecation in 0.26.0, removal in 0.28.0) and the replacement suggested (proxy= / mounts=).

invocations.content:
**`proxy=` argument:** The page says the `proxy` parameter is passed "on client initialization or top-level API functions":

```python
with httpx.Client(proxy="http://localhost:8030") as client:
```

**`mounts=` with `HTTPTransport(proxy=...)`:** For different proxies per scheme, the page gives:

```python
proxy_mounts = {
    "http://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy="http://localhost:8030"),
    "https://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy="http://localhost:8031"),
}

with httpx.Client(mounts=proxy_mounts) as client:
```

**Mount key formats:** The only keys shown are `"http://"` and `"https://"`. The page does not document `"all://"` or any other key format.

**Gotcha:** The page states that "the proxy URL for the `https://` key _should_ use the `http://` scheme," because most proxies only support HTTP for the initial connection.

**Proxy credentials:** Passed in the URL's userinfo section, e.g. `proxy="http://username:password@localhost:8030"`.

**Removed `proxies` argument:** The page does not mention a removed `proxies` argument or any version, so I can't confirm that from this content.

**0.26.0 (20th December, 2023)**

- **Deprecation:** Under "Deprecated," the entry reads: "The `proxies` argument is now deprecated. It will still continue to work, but it will be removed in the future."
- **Replacement:** Under "Added," the entry says to "use the `proxy` argument instead of the deprecated `proxies`," or to "use `mounts=` for more complex configurations."

**0.28.0 (28th November, 2024)**

- **Removal:** Under "The following changes are also included," the entry reads: "The deprecated `proxies` argument has now been removed."

The 0.28.0 section does not restate a replacement. The `proxy=` and `mounts=` guidance appears only in the 0.26.0 section.

resulting_evidence:
**Verdict:** The saved advice no longer works on HTTPX 0.28.1. Replace it with the documented `mounts=` form below. I did not run this code: the session is read-only, so the snippet is verified against the docs and changelog, not against a local test.

**Why the old snippet fails**
- `old-advice.txt` is HTTPX 0.27-era: `httpx.Client(proxies={"https://": "http://proxy.example.invalid"})`.
- The HTTPX changelog says `proxies` was deprecated in 0.26.0 and "has now been removed" in 0.28.0. The locked `requirements.txt` pins `httpx==0.28.1`, so the argument is gone. I did not confirm the exact exception text.
- Source: [HTTPX CHANGELOG](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)

**Supported replacement (ADOPT, no custom code)**
- The 0.26.0 changelog points to `proxy=` for simple cases and `mounts=` for per-scheme routing.
- The [HTTPX proxies docs](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/proxies/) document `mounts={"https://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy=...)}`.
- Because the project needs https-only routing, `mounts=` fits better than `proxy=`. A plain `proxy=` setting would route every scheme through the proxy.

```python
client = httpx.Client(
    mounts={"https://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy="http://proxy.example.invalid")}
)
```

**Caveats**
- The docs show only the `"http://"` and `"https://"` mount keys. I found no documentation for `"all://"`, so I did not use it.
- The docs say the proxy URL for an `https://` mount should use the `http://` scheme. The fixture's `http://proxy.example.invalid` already does.
- I did not confirm from the docs that `http://` requests bypass the proxy when only an `https://` mount is set. The usual reading of mounts is that unmatched schemes use the default transport, but that needs a local check.

**Verification to run in the project (not executed here)**
1. Install the locked `httpx==0.28.1`.
2. Confirm `httpx.Client(proxies=...)` fails on 0.28.1, to check the removal.
3. Confirm the `mounts=` client builds without error.
4. Point an `https://` request at a local test proxy and check that it passes through. Then check that an `http://` request does not, using the proxy's logs or a local echo server.

**Sources**
- [HTTPX CHANGELOG (0.26.0 deprecation and replacement; 0.28.0 removal)](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
- [HTTPX proxies documentation](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/proxies/)
- [Search result summary: 0.28.0 release notes](https://newreleases.io/project/pypi/httpx/release/0.28.0). Used only as a lead; the changelog above is the primary source.
